page: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dalsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 160 vCPUs across 80 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is configured with 320.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 14,528.43 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 463.81 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server also demonstrates top-tier throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving.

The primary tradeoff of the D160als_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per core and the absence of local storage, which makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or massive in-memory caching. However, its high compute density and top-tier CPU performance make it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads. This resource profile is optimal for CPU-intensive tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, large-scale text and image processing, and LLM inference, where it achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds.
